title: "Week 4 application: which attractor features survive resolution?"
subtitle: "Completing the state-space example"
toc: true
---

## Scientific question

Which connected or loop-like features of a sampled state-space representation
remain distinguishable over a range of neighbourhood scales, and which are
short-lived consequences of sampling or one threshold?

## Carrying forward the Week 3 construction

Use the same sampled trajectory, state-space point cloud, metric and Rips
filtration introduced in the [Week 3 attractor example](../week-03/case-study.qmd).
Persistent homology now applies $H_p(-;\mathbb F_2)$ at every scale and retains
the maps induced by complex inclusion.

The diagram is therefore the endpoint of a chain of choices:

$$
\text{trajectory}\to\text{point cloud}\to
\{K_\varepsilon\}\to
\{H_p(K_\varepsilon;\mathbb F_2)\}\to D_p.
$$

## What would be inspected

For $H_0$, inspect the scales over which components remain separate before
merging. For $H_1$, inspect whether loop classes live across a substantial
range of resolutions. Link any candidate class back to the point cloud using a
representative-cycle diagnostic, while remembering that representatives are
not unique.

## Baseline and sensitivity

Compare with recurrence, spectral or geometric summaries appropriate to the
system. Repeat the complete pipeline after changing sampling density, noise,
coordinate scaling, metric and delay-coordinate parameters. A long interval
is useful only if its interpretation survives relevant upstream choices.

## Interpretation boundary

A persistent $H_1$ class supports the statement that a loop in the chosen
complex filtration remains distinguishable across scale. It does not alone
establish a periodic orbit, a particular invariant set or a causal mechanism.
Those conclusions require temporal and dynamical evidence.

::: {.callout-note title="Planned data extension"}
No empirical attractor result is claimed here. This is the point where a later
real-data example is needed: it should publish the observations, preprocessing,
metric, filtration range, baseline and sensitivity analysis together rather
than showing only a final barcode.
:::
